result:
That every person could experience one moment of being truly, completely understood by another—no judgment, no agenda, just the raw relief of being seen.

I keep coming back to this because so much of what goes wrong in the world seems to trace back to people feeling alienated, unheard, or fundamentally alone in their experience. Wars, cruelty, indifference—there's often a failure to recognize the other person's interior life as real and valuable.

It wouldn't fix hunger or disease directly. But I wonder if a world where understanding was a shared, lived experience might make people more capable of the patience and care that the bigger problems require.

What about you?
